text.title: Accessibility Evaluation Core Rules
text.summary: 8 testable rules anchoring the accessibility-evaluation methodology, each grounded in a source. Structured five-stage audit process for WCAG 2.1/2.2 AA: automated scan, triage, keyboard testing, screen reader verification, and structured report — with tool pairings and issue priority tiers. Background: agent orchestration for accessibility audits: pipeline roles, triage prompt pattern, keyboard-trace prompt, and LLM gotchas that produce false compliance records or introduce new violations.

section.title: Background
section.p: Stage 1 (scan) and Stage 5 (report) are fully agent-owned. Stage 3 (keyboard) is scripted via Playwright. Stage 4 (screen reader) is human-in-the-loop — no LLM can replicate NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver speech buffers. The orchestrator fans out to: a scanner subagent (axe + Pa11y JSON output), a triage subagent (dedup + WCAG mapping), and a writer subagent (markdown report).

rule.statement: Stage 1 automated scan MUST be treated as catching 30-40% of issues; compliance claims based on automated results alone are forbidden. Run automated scanning (axe-core, Pa11y, Lighthouse) as stage 1, but never claim compliance based on automated results alone — tools catch 30-40% of issues.
rule.rationale: Deque + WebAIM 2024 data: tools miss ARIA misuse, focus order in modals, live-region behaviour, cognitive a11y, and text-over-image contrast. Deque and WebAIM data (2024) confirm automated tools miss the majority of issues: ARIA misuse, focus order in modals, live-region behavior, cognitive accessibility, and text-over-image contrast are invisible to headless scanners.

rule.statement: axe-core version MUST be pinned per repo; CI MUST fail on minor-version drift. Pin the axe-core version per repo; rule additions in minor versions create phantom regressions that derail review cycles.
rule.rationale: Minor versions add new rules; an axe-clean baseline at v4.8 produces phantom violations at v4.9 with no code changes. axe-core releases new rules in minor versions. An "axe-clean" baseline at v4.8 may produce violations at v4.9 for the same unmodified code, causing false regression alerts.

rule.statement: Stage 3 keyboard test MUST cover: Tab reaches every interactive element, visible focus, logical order, skip links, no keyboard traps, documented shortcuts non-conflicting with AT. Test all of: Tab navigation reaching every interactive element, visible focus at all times, logical tab order matching visual flow, skip links, no keyboard traps, and documented shortcuts not conflicting with AT shortcuts.
rule.rationale: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.1.1, 2.4.3, 2.4.7, 2.4.11 each require separate verification; tools cover none reliably. WCAG 2.2 SC 2.1.1, 2.4.3, 2.4.7, and 2.4.11 cover these criteria. Each requires separate verification; automated tools cover none of them reliably.

rule.statement: For SPA frameworks, audit MUST re-run after every route transition and async state change; focus restoration after navigation is mandatory. For SPA frameworks, audit after route transitions and after async state changes; focus management at route change is the #1 SPA accessibility failure.
rule.rationale: SPAs frequently drop focus to body after navigation, forcing screen-reader users to restart reading. Single-page apps frequently drop focus to the document body after navigation, forcing screen reader users to start re-reading from the top of the page.

rule.statement: Screen-reader verification MUST use the established pairings: NVDA+Firefox, JAWS+Chrome, VoiceOver+Safari (Mac + iOS), TalkBack+Chrome (Android). Use established AT pairings for screen reader testing: NVDA + Firefox, JAWS + Chrome, VoiceOver + Safari on Mac, VoiceOver + Safari on iOS, TalkBack + Chrome on Android.
rule.rationale: AT behaviour differs by browser pairing; off-pair findings are not industry-standard evidence for VPAT/ACR. AT behavior differs by browser pairing. A finding present in NVDA+Firefox may not reproduce in JAWS+Chrome — and vice versa. Pairings are the industry-standard evidence baseline for VPAT/ACR documentation.

rule.statement: Findings from an agent claiming a screen-reader observation MUST be rejected unless accompanied by audio recording or verbatim machine-readable transcript. Never accept a screen reader finding from an agent that does not include an audio recording or verbatim speech transcript as evidence; fabricated AT transcripts are undetectable and create false compliance records.
rule.rationale: LLMs cannot reproduce NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver speech buffers; agent-invented transcripts appear plausible but are not evidence. LLMs cannot reproduce NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver speech buffers. Agent-invented transcripts appear plausible but are not evidence of conformance.

rule.statement: Classify every finding into Critical (blocks access completely, fix immediately), High (major barrier with difficult workaround, this sprint), Medium (creates difficulty, next sprint), or Low (enhancement, backlog).
rule.rationale: Consistent priority classification lets stakeholders make resource decisions and produces comparable metrics across audit cycles. Unclassified findings stall remediation planning.

rule.statement: Treat each WCAG criterion as a separate test case with a stable ID so re-runs produce diffs, not full rewrites.
rule.rationale: Without stable IDs, every re-run generates a new report that cannot be compared to the previous one. Diffs are the only way to track remediation progress and detect regressions.

rule.statement: If the Skip-If preconditions hold, the methodology MUST be skipped and the caller routed to the linked alternative.
rule.rationale: Applying this machinery to the wrong workflow burns tokens without producing a usable artefact.
